title: What a Race Entry Actually Costs Across Southeast Asia
seo_title: Race Entry Fees in Southeast Asia: 219 Races Compared in USD
meta_description: Entry fees for 219 Southeast Asian road races converted to US dollars: typical prices by country and distance, the cheapest and most expensive races, and how early-bird tiers work.
dek: Most road races in Southeast Asia charge between about US$27 and US$41 for their headline distance, and many cost less. Singapore is in a different bracket. Here are the entry fees of 219 races, converted to one currency and compared by country and distance.

sections.heading: What the numbers cover
paragraphs: Run SEA's race calendar records an entry-fee range for 219 of its 446 races, as each organiser published it. They span race dates from June 2026 to September 2027, and 149 of the races were still to come on 6 November 2026 [1]. The fees are in nine currencies, led by Thai baht (59 races), Philippine pesos (51), ringgit (44), rupiah (31) and dong (25).

To compare them, every fee here is converted to US dollars at the European Central Bank's euro reference rates of 5 November 2026: US$1 = SGD 1.277, MYR 4.046, PHP 63.0, THB 33.44 and IDR 18,069 [2]. The dong is not in the ECB set, so it uses 25,692 dong to the dollar from ExchangeRate-API on 6 November 2026 [3]. The Brunei dollar is exchanged at par with the Singapore dollar [4].

A range usually runs from the cheapest distance to the dearest, so its bottom is roughly the cheapest way into the race (often a 5K or fun run) and its top is usually the headline distance. Some ranges instead span early-bird and regular prices, or local and international entries. Three races list only a 'from' price and are left out of the top-of-range figures.

sections.heading: The typical fee: about US$33 at the top of the range
paragraphs: Across all 219 races, the median bottom of the range is US$15 and the median top is US$33. Half of all races top out between US$27 and US$41 [1].

Distance moves the price, but less than you might expect. At the 69 races whose headline distance is the marathon (and which publish a top price), the median top of the range is US$40. At the 147 races built around the half marathon it is US$30 [1].

Where organisers list a price for each distance, the steps are visible. VPBank Hanoi International Marathon's standard prices were 1,668,000 dong (about US$65) for the 42K, 1,268,000 (US$49) for the 21K, 988,000 (US$38) for the 10K and 668,000 (US$26) for the 5K. Borobudur Marathon lists IDR 950,000 (US$53) for the full, 850,000 (US$47) for the half and 650,000 (US$36) for the 10K. Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok lists THB 1,400 to 1,800 (US$42 to US$54) for the marathon and 1,200 to 1,600 for the half [1]. In all three, the marathon is the cheapest distance per kilometre.

sections.heading: Country by country
paragraphs: Singapore is the outlier. Its four races with fees have a median top of about US$117, and the BYD Singapore International Marathon lists SGD 98 to 208, or US$77 to US$163 [1].

Elsewhere the medians sit close together. The median top of the range is US$37 in Vietnam (959,000 dong, 25 races), US$35 in Thailand (THB 1,175, 60 races), US$32 in the Philippines (PHP 2,000, 51 races), US$30 in Indonesia (IDR 550,000, 31 races) and US$28 in Malaysia (RM 114, 44 races) [1].

The marathon-led races show more difference. Their median top is US$59 in Indonesia (6 races), US$44 in Vietnam (10), US$40 in the Philippines (17), US$37 in Malaysia (9) and US$36 in Thailand (25) [1]. Thailand has the most marathons on the calendar and some of the cheapest: Chombueng Marathon tops out at THB 1,000 (US$30) and the Bangkok Marathon at THB 1,250 (US$37).
Malaysia has the cheapest way in. Its median bottom of range is about US$11 (RM 45), because many Malaysian races add a short distance priced from RM 25 to RM 45 [1].

sections.heading: The most and least expensive
paragraphs: The highest tops in the data are the Singapore Marathon (US$163), Forest Run at Sentosa (SGD 175, US$137), the Jakarta International Marathon (IDR 1,814,900, about US$100), Garmin Run Singapore (SGD 125, US$98 for the 21K) and Thailand's POCARI SWEAT Run Carnival (THB 3,090, US$92). The Dili International Marathon in Timor-Leste charges international runners US$90 for the full and US$45 for the half, and is free for Timorese nationals [1].

At the cheap end, Cyberjaya 21K charged a flat RM 60 (US$15) and Kathu Marathon in Phuket THB 200 to 700 (US$6 to US$21). Sarawak Energy Marathon's early-bird price for the 42 km was RM 90 (US$22). A few community runs are cheaper still: NasDem Run for Change in Indonesia listed entries from free to IDR 100,000 (US$6) [1].

sections.heading: Early-bird tiers are worth it
paragraphs: Many organisers raise prices in steps as race day approaches. Jitra Half Marathon in Kedah charged RM 80, 65 and 50 for its 21 km, 10 km and 5 km until 31 May 2026, then RM 95, 85 and 65 from June to July, so the 21 km rose by RM 15 (19%). Pink Run: The Half Marathon in Cavite lists its 21K at PHP 1,450 until 20 December 2026 and PHP 1,600 after. Hue Amazing Marathon's 42K ran from 799,000 to 1,569,000 dong across its price phases [1].

In these examples, entering early saves from about 10% to nearly half on the same distance. Check, too, whether the published price is the final one: Larian Kita Jubli Perak in Malaysia, for one, lists its fees plus an admin fee [1].

sections.heading: Using these numbers
paragraphs: Treat these figures as a guide to what is normal, not as a price list. Organisers change fees between editions and between phases, and the range a race publishes may be early-bird only, regular only or both. The entry page for each race has its current price.

For a race abroad, compare the whole trip rather than the entry alone: travel and a night or two near the start come on top of every fee here. Choose the race first, then enter in its cheapest tier. Runners weighing an organised trip can read the guide to race-travel packages at runsea.run/articles/using-a-race-travel-agency-when-a-package-is-worth-it/.

faqs.question: How much does a race entry cost in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Across 219 races in Run SEA's calendar, the median top of each race's fee range is about US$33 and half of races top out between US$27 and US$41. Marathon-led races have a median top of about US$40 and half-marathon races about US$30. Singapore is far higher, with a median top near US$117.

faqs.question: Which Southeast Asian country has the cheapest race entries?
faqs.answer: Malaysia has the lowest typical prices, with a median top of range of about US$28 (RM 114) and short distances from RM 25 to RM 45. Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand are close behind, between about US$30 and US$35. Singapore is the most expensive.

faqs.question: How much is a marathon entry in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: At races led by the marathon, the median top of the fee range is about US$40, from around US$36 in Thailand to US$59 in Indonesia. Examples include the Bangkok Marathon at up to THB 1,250 (US$37), VPBank Hanoi at 1,668,000 dong (US$65) and Singapore at up to SGD 208 (US$163).

editorial_notes: Rewritten 6 Nov 2026 as a data piece on the price_range field of data/entities (219 races). Ranges were parsed to a low and high per race (3 'from' prices have no high) and converted to USD: ECB reference rates of 5 Nov 2026 (USD 1.1224, SGD 1.4336, MYR 4.5412, PHP 70.706, THB 37.533, IDR 20,281.15 per EUR), VND 25,692.44 per USD from ExchangeRate-API (6 Nov 2026), BND at par with SGD (MAS). Category (marathon vs half) is the race's headline distance. Backpacker-blog travel budgets from the old version dropped; no travel-cost figures are given because none could be sourced.
